title: Protected branch-name list duplicated across filter expressions
description: The literal ["main", "master", "develop"] is written twice in the derived-state block (otherBranches exclusion at line 217 and protectedBranches definition at line 219) and the same concept is hand-maintained against the backend's protected-branch set. Duplicating the literal risks drift (one filter updated, the other not), and the two filters are computed by re-scanning `branches` independently. Extract a single `const PROTECTED = new Set(["main", "master", "develop"])` (module-level constant) and reference it in both filters.
evidence: Line 217: `otherBranches = branches.filter((b) => !b.is_yours && !b.is_archived && !["main", "master", "develop"].includes(b.name))`; line 219: `protectedBranches = branches.filter((b) => ["main", "master", "develop"].includes(b.name))`. Same array literal in two places.
est_reduction: ~2 lines net plus removal of a drift hazard
behavior_preservation: Pure refactor: identical membership test via a shared Set/array; output of both filters unchanged.
